No existing reference for the "percent contribution change" pattern, but this question passed cleanly on the first try. The reasoning was straightforward:

- pct_contribution(year) = individual income taxes / total receipts × 100
- change = pct(2011) − pct(2012)... actually pct(2011) − pct(2010)

The CY2010→CY2011 receipts data for individual income taxes and total budget receipts is standard and the arithmetic is simple percent-of-total. This is a clean, well-trodden pattern with no new gotchas — no page-offset surprise, no unit scaling trap, no rounding-stage ambiguity, no sign error. The existing main skill already covers locating receipts tables and unit conventions.

The only mildly generalizable point is that "change in percent contribution" questions resolve as a difference of two ratios (not a relative diff, not a ratio of ratios), and the sign convention follows later-year minus earlier-year. But that's already standard arithmetic that I got right without needing a reminder, and my memory already documents the trickier RELATIVE-diff and percent-of-total variants.

No new generalizable lesson was exposed by this question. It passed on the standard approach with no friction.
